CellEdgeR technical note

technical-note.Rmd

Brief Intro

CellEdgeR builds Delaunay graphs from spatial cell coordinates, counts label-based motifs, and tests differential abundance with edgeR using Chung-Lu-style volume offsets. The default and primary statistical model is volume based.

CellEdgeR tests two result sets:

  • edges: edge motifs extracted with top_edges().
  • motifs2: wedge and triangle motifs extracted with top_motifs2().

Node counts are used internally for exposure and submotif values, but nodes are not tested. Wedges and triangles are kept separate; there is no merged TP_* triplet test.

Quick Start 

library(CellEdgeR)

samples_list <- make_demo_samples(n_cells = 2000, seed = 1)
metadata_df <- data.frame(
  condition = rep(c("ctrl", "treated"), each = length(samples_list) / 2),
  row.names = names(samples_list)
)

cellgraph <- build_cell_graphs(samples_list, n_cores = 2)
cellgraph <- count_motifs_graphs(cellgraph, max_edge_len = 50, include_wedge = TRUE, n_cores = 2)
cellgraph <- motif_edger(
  cellgraph,
  sample_df = metadata_df,
  design_formula = "~ condition"
)

top_edges(cellgraph, coef = "conditiontreated")
top_motifs2(cellgraph, coef = "conditiontreated")

Motif Layers

For each sample, CellEdgeR builds a Delaunay triangulation on the 2D coordinates and treats unique edges as candidate adjacency. Optional pruning by max_edge_len removes long edges before counting motifs.

Motifs are counted by label:

  • Nodes: N_<label>, used internally but not tested by motif_edger().
  • Edges: E_<label1>_<label2>, unordered.
  • Triangles: T_<label1>_<label2>_<label3>, unordered.
  • Wedges: W_<center>_<leaf1>_<leaf2>, centered and optional.

Counts are per sample, yielding a motif-by-sample matrix for each layer.

Volume Offsets

The volume approach uses label-specific degree volumes to represent how much of the graph is available for each label in each sample. For a label, the volume is the sum of degrees of cells with that label. Let 2m be twice the number of edges in the sample.

Offsets are log expected counts under a Chung-Lu-style graph with preserved label volumes:

  • Edges: log(vol_a) + log(vol_b) - log(2m), with a -log(2) correction for same-label unordered pairs.
  • Triangles: log(vol_a) + log(vol_b) + log(vol_c) - 2 * log(2m), plus an unordered-label multiplicity correction.
  • Wedges: center exposure from sum(degree * (degree - 1)) for the center label, leaf-label volumes, and an equal-leaf correction.

The offsets use a small offset_pseudo to avoid log(0).

Differential Model

motif_edger() stacks edge, wedge, and triangle counts and fits a single edgeR quasi-likelihood negative-binomial GLM with volume offsets. The design matrix comes from design_formula and can include multiple covariates:

cellgraph <- motif_edger(
  cellgraph,
  sample_df = sample_df,
  design_formula = "~ condition + batch"
)

edges_tbl <- top_edges(cellgraph, coef = "conditiontreated")
motifs2_tbl <- top_motifs2(cellgraph, coef = "conditiontreated")

The logFC is interpreted as a differential motif rate after correcting for the volume exposure. The p-value is a model coefficient test, not a direct test of raw counts or normalized-count medians.

Before fitting, CellEdgeR applies edgeR::filterByExpr() to the stacked edge/wedge/triangle count matrix. This is the standard edgeR low-expression filter and prevents motifs observed in too few samples, including one-sample spikes, from entering the multiple-testing table. The filtering summary is stored in cellgraph$edger$filter.

Motif2 Submotif Columns

top_motifs2() returns wedges and triangles in one table. It also adds the edge submotifs implied by each three-label motif:

  • edge12, edge13, edge23.
  • edge12_logFC, edge13_logFC, edge23_logFC.
  • edge12_PValue, edge13_PValue, edge23_PValue.
  • edge12_FDR, edge13_FDR, edge23_FDR.
  • submotif_min_FDR and submotif_max_abs_logFC.

For wedges, label 1 is the center. edge12 and edge13 are the center-leaf edges, while edge23 is the leaf-leaf closing edge.

Required Inputs

  1. cells_by_sample: a named list of data frames. Each data frame must have:
    • Column 1: numeric x coordinate.
    • Column 2: numeric y coordinate.
    • Column 3: label, character or factor.
  2. sample_df: a data frame with one row per sample and row names equal to names(cells_by_sample).

Build Graphs And Count Motifs 

cellgraph <- build_cell_graphs(cells_by_sample, n_cores = 4)
cellgraph <- count_motifs_graphs(
  cellgraph,
  max_edge_len = 50,
  include_wedge = TRUE,
  n_cores = 4
)

Choose A Delaunay Cutoff

Inspect the edge-length distribution and choose a cutoff that removes the long tail while keeping local neighbors. The cutoff is in the same units as your coordinates.

edge_lengths <- unlist(lapply(cellgraph$per_sample_graph, function(ps) ps$edge_len))

ggplot2::ggplot(data.frame(edge_len = edge_lengths), ggplot2::aes(edge_len)) +
  ggplot2::geom_density(fill = "#4477aa", alpha = 0.3, color = "#223355") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_log10("Edge length (log scale)") +
  ggplot2::ylab("Density") +
  ggplot2::ggtitle("Edge length distribution (density, log-x)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

Motif Space Size

motif_space_size() summarizes the number of possible tested edge, triangle, and wedge label motifs:

motif_space_size(cellgraph)

Plotting Motifs

Spatial plot of a motif within a sample:

plot_sample_graph(
  cellgraph,
  sample_name = "s1",
  max_edge_len = 50,
  motif_key = "T_a_b_c",
  motif_node_size = 0.8
)

Quantification of motifs across samples:

norm_df <- get_motif_values(cellgraph, value = "norm")
df_plot <- data.frame(sample = rownames(norm_df), value = norm_df[["T_a_b_c"]])
df_plot <- merge(df_plot, sample_df, by.x = "sample", by.y = "row.names", all.x = TRUE)

ggplot2::ggplot(df_plot, ggplot2::aes(x = condition, y = value, fill = condition)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.6) +
  ggplot2::ylab("Normalized motif count (volume offset)") +
  ggplot2::xlab("condition")

Assumptions

  • Delaunay edges are a reasonable proxy for spatial adjacency in each sample.
  • Pruning by max_edge_len removes long-range edges without removing meaningful local adjacency.
  • Cell labels are accurate and consistent across samples.
  • Samples are independent, and motif counts follow a negative-binomial model.
  • Volume offsets approximate expected counts under a graph with preserved label degree volumes and total edge count.
